To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the WMAP 3-year catalogue is a good sample of sources with rising spectral index at high frequency, but that the VSA flux-density estimates are systematically lower than WMAP for the fainter objects, and that this is due to Eddington bias.
the WMAP 3-year catalogue of point sources is dominated by sources with flat to rising spectra and that these sources are variable.

the spectral indices between 13.75 and 33 GHz for sources in the WMAP 3-year catalogue are typically positive, and that there is good agreement between the flux densities of the brighter sources in this sample and those of WMAP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the sources detected in the 3-yr WMAP point source catalogue.
the properties of extragalactic radio sources at high frequency.

the study of the properties of a sample of extragalactic radio sources, selected from the 3-year data of the WMAP satellite, and observed in the frequency range 13.9-33.75 GHz with the Very-Long-Baseline Array and with the Very Small-Array.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sources are a mixture of blazars, radio galaxies and star-forming galaxies.
the WMAP catalogue is not complete to 5σ at 33 GHz, but is very close to complete to 5 σ at 16 GHz.
the sources in the sample have a wide range of spectral properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WMAP data at 33 GHz have a large number of sources with spectra which are significantly different from those of the well-known bright radio sources.
the WMAP 3-year data catalogue contains a large number of sources that are very different from the bright sources that have previously dominated the extragalactic sky.
the WMAP 3-year point source catalogue is reliable for the brighter sources (S 33 > 1 Jy), but for the fainter ones, the flux densities should be treated with caution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WMAP catalogue is a good representation of the sky at 33 GHz, and the sources it contains are a good sample of extragalactic radio sources at that frequency.
, for the sources we observed, the 33-GHz WMAP flux-density measurements are not reliable, and the WMAP 3-year catalogue should be regarded as a preliminary source catalogue.
, at these flux densities, the extragalactic sky is not dominated by the same sources as at lower frequencies.
